blocks.tamil_translation: he set out at night taking the Sadaqah. (Without knowing) he gave that Sadaqah to an adulteress. The next morning it was talked about among the people, “Last night Sadaqah was given to an adulteress.' He said, “O Allah! All praise is for You alone (for the Sadaqah reaching) an adulteress” (my wealth was not even worthy of that!). Then (for the third time) he resolved, “Tonight I will certainly give Sadaqah.” Accordingly, he set out at night taking the Sadaqah and placed it in the hand of a rich man. The next morning it was talked about among the people, “Last night Sadaqah was given to a wealthy man.' The one who gave the Sadaqah said, “O Allah! All praise is for You alone for making the Sadaqah reach a thief, an adulteress and a wealthy man! (My wealth was not even worthy of being given to such people.) In a dream he was told, (Your Sadaqah has been accepted.) “(The reason your Sadaqah was made to be given) to the thief was only so that he might reform, make Tawbah and give up stealing! It was made to be given to the adulteress so that she might make Tawbah from adultery, and so that, seeing that Allah Ta'ala has given to her even without committing adultery, she would feel a sense of shame. It was made to be given to the wealthy man so that he might take a lesson (from how the servants of Allah Ta'ala give Sadaqah secretly) and he too might spend (in the path of Allah Ta'ala) from the wealth Allah Ta'ala has given him,”” Rasulullah ﷺ said, Hazrat Abu Hurairah (RA) narrates.

blocks.text: Explanation:- Because of that man's pure intention, all three Sadaqahs
